long_biography.plain_text:
Thomas Leclercq spent seven years in operating roles across Auchan, Norauto, Kiabi and Decathlon, learning retail through stores and customer-facing work rather than formal business school. A member of Decathlon's founding family, he held shares in the sporting-goods retailer before divesting his initial family holdings and pursuing investments independently.

He turned towards US technology companies in the late 1990s, seeking platforms positioned for durable shifts in consumer and business behaviour. In 2010, Leclercq created Leclercq American Capital, whose present focus includes cybersecurity, advanced computing, biotechnology and medical technology. Its approach combines private equity and growth capital with selective public-market holdings, favouring patient ownership of businesses with defensible products.
